question: What does mode mean?
answer: mode in file handling refers to the mode string used when opening a file, indicating how the file is used such as "r" for read, "w" for write, or "a" for append [S1].

S2.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
S2.text: 1. Descriptive Statistics Descriptive statistics summarize a dataset. Measures of central tendency are the mean (the sum of the values divided by the number of values), the median (the middle value of the sorted data) and the mode (the most frequent value). The mean is sensitive to outliers; the median is robust to them. For right-skewed data such as incomes the mean is usually larger than the median. Measures of spread describe variability. The range is maximum minus minimum. The variance averages squared deviations from the mean, and the standard deviation is the square root of the variance, so it has the same units as the data. The interquartile range (IQR) is Q3 minus Q1 and is used to flag outliers: a common rule marks values below Q1 - 1.5 * IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 * IQR. Population variance divides the sum of squared deviations by N, the population size. Sample

Ensemble: combining several models; bagging reduces variance, boosting reduces bias. Clustering: grouping unlabeled examples; k-means assigns each point to the nearest of k centroids. PCA: principal component analysis, a linear technique for dimensionality reduction.

S4.title: Ml Reference Notes
S4.text: Feature: an input variable used by a model, for example a person's age. Label or target: the value the model should predict. Hyperparameter: a setting chosen before training, such as the learning rate, tree depth or number of neighbors k. Parameter: a value learned during training, such as the weights of linear regression. Epoch: one full pass through the training data. Batch size: the number of examples used for one gradient update. Learning rate: the step size of gradient descent. Regularization: a penalty that discourages overly complex models. L2 (ridge) shrinks weights; L1 (lasso) can set weights to zero. Overfitting: low training error but high validation error because the model memorized noise. Underfitting: high error on both training and validation data because the model is too simple. Bias: error from wrong or overly simple assumptions.
